chosen.title: opening curtains to bright sunshine
chosen.faces: none (back view only; face never turns to camera within 5.6-8.8s)
chosen.why: Static 16:9 shot from behind a woman in a white tee who parts dark brown curtains; 5.6s first sliver of light, 6.0-8.0s curtains swing open and warm blown-out daylight floods the frame over her hands and shoulders. Low-saturation brown/white palette, natural light, no logos or text, gentle continuous motion that fills a 3.2s cut. Not POV and no blanket, so it reads as 'someone opens the curtains' rather than 'my hand opens the curtains'.

alternates.why: Heavily defocused warm sun glowing through a sheer curtain, 1080p, no people at all. Very film-like and low-saturation but almost no movement and no hand; usable only as a soft light-texture insert or a dissolve layer, not as the curtain-opening action.

Silhouette from behind throws open hotel curtains onto a grey city skyline (0.4-3.0s). Faceless and calm, but cold overcast light and an urban view clash with the warm morning tone; distant fallback only.

notes: Multi-word queries (morning light curtains / hand curtain sunlight / waking up morning light bed) returned zero results on Mixkit; single-word 'curtains', 'sunlight window' and 'morning bed' sheets were reviewed instead. No true POV hand-on-curtain clip exists in the free library; 22101 was pitch black, 23505 has garish striped curtains, 21669/23500/23310 show faces or hotel interiors. 22066 is a legitimate faceless curtain-opening beat with warm light, but if the POV/hand-on-blanket framing is essential, the cream paper card is the cleaner substitute. Highlights are clipped after ~8.2s (window blows out to pure white), so a slight exposure pull-down or a fade may help match the film look.
